verdict.root_cause: The ad service stopped serving at 20:59:11 and never came back. Its own logs show a cold start at 20:58:05, four normal ad requests through 20:59:10 with intact trace context and no errors, then a JVM-driven gRPC shutdown at 20:59:11 followed by total silence across the 21:00:16 alert [tr_ce520f9e7393]. Tempo holds no ad spans at all for the window [tr_2178f15d99cb]. Ad's own output never complains about an unreachable peer, a full disk, a wrong address or credential, or memory pressure — it simply goes quiet after a signalled stop, which is the silent-culprit signature. Ad's only change records are first-creation entries by platform-automation, not a rollout, config edit, or limit change [tr_03b9ea884053], and flagd came up cleanly, parsed its flag file, and logged no reload or evaluation errors [tr_f75ff8f53156, tr_df44850fa5b2]. The mechanism now is a stopped ad process behind a still-advertised service endpoint; the fix is to bring ad back up.
verdict.reasoning: The only positive, dated signal on the board is ad's log timeline [tr_ce520f9e7393]: serving normally until 20:59:10, shutdown at 20:59:11, then nothing emitted at or near onset. Silence with no self-reported cause separates a stopped process from a network partition (which logs unreachable peers) and from disk_fill or bad_config (which name no-space or a wrong address). The empty Tempo result corroborates rather than adds: nothing served means nothing exported [tr_2178f15d99cb]. No competing act exists in the change log for ad [tr_03b9ea884053], and flagd is cleared as an active actor — creation-only records with no flag mutation, one clean startup, successful config parse, and fault-injection flags aimed at cart and payment rather than ad [tr_df44850fa5b2, tr_f75ff8f53156]. Both Prometheus queries returned structural unavailability, not observed zeros [tr_1c44b72de6bd, tr_f2b13604310b], and product-catalog's log query was substring-filtered to 'error', so it is neither implicated nor cleared [tr_181fc5b26702]. Ad is named because it is the only service with a demonstrated transition from serving to silent immediately before onset.
open_questions: What signalled the 20:59:11 shutdown, and did the container restart afterwards? No pod state, restart count, or exit code was retrieved, which is why this is medium confidence.

Do ad's callers hang to a deadline or fail fast with connection-refused? No caller-side traces or socket evidence was collected, and that distinction separates a frozen-but-listening process from a dead one.

Why did product-catalog alert at the same second? Its unfiltered logs were never queried and its span metrics do not exist, so no causal link from ad has been shown and a shared upstream trigger is untested.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad JVM, capped at a 200m max heap, exhausted memory and was terminated, leaving it unable to serve.
alternatives.why_not: The 20:59:11 termination is an orderly shutdown hook completing with a clean server-shutdown line, not the abrupt truncation an OOM-kill leaves, and no memory error appears [tr_ce520f9e7393]; no resource-limit change is recorded either [tr_03b9ea884053].

alternatives.root_cause: A flagd fault-injection flag enabled at provisioning drove failures in a service downstream of ad's call path.
alternatives.why_not: No flag-value mutation is recorded and no hot-reload or evaluation error appears in flagd's logs; the enabled fault flags target cart and payment, and ad's failure is its own process being silent rather than a failing flagged path [tr_df44850fa5b2, tr_f75ff8f53156].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating ad's container should end the log silence that has held since 20:59:11. Within roughly one JVM cold start (the previous one took ~17s from first line to 'listening on gRPC port' [tr_ce520f9e7393]) Loki on {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"ad-..."} should show a fresh startup sequence followed by ordinary per-request ad lines carrying populated trace ids, and no further 'gRPC shutdown / JVM shutdown' line. Note the confirmation must be log-based: ad emits no trace-derived span metrics, so error-ratio and latency percentiles do not exist for it in Prometheus [tr_1c44b72de6bd], and Tempo held no ad spans at all [tr_2178f15d99cb] — if spans do reappear in Tempo after the restart that is a bonus signal, not a required one.
proposal.if_wrong: Three falsifiers. (1) No startup lines appear within five minutes — the container is not being scheduled, and the mechanism is at the orchestrator, not the process. (2) Startup lines appear and are followed within a minute or two by another JVM-driven graceful shutdown — something external is signalling ad to stop (the open question of what sent the 20:59:11 signal was never answered; no pod state, restart count, or exit code was retrieved), and repeating the restart will just churn. (3) ad logs resume and serve normally but product-catalog is still alerting — the causal link from ad to product-catalog was never shown (its unfiltered logs were never queried [tr_181fc5b26702], its span metrics do not exist [tr_f2b13604310b]), so a shared upstream trigger would remain live and this restart would have fixed a symptom.
proposal.risk: restart_service is not reversible. If the 20:59:11 stop was commanded by something still in force — an operator-driven teardown, a scheduler eviction, a supervisor — the recreate either fails or is undone, and we have spent the one irreversible action while learning less than a pod-state/exit-code query would have told us for free. If ad was in fact already restarted by the platform after 20:59:11 (unverified), this recreate interrupts a working process and causes a second, self-inflicted outage window. It also discards in-process state; for ad that is cache only, so the cost is a cold cache and slower first responses, not data. And it closes off post-mortem inspection of the stopped container's exit code.
proposal.blast_radius: One service for the duration of the recreate. This brief names only ad's outbound edge (ad → flagd), not its callers, so the inbound set is not fully enumerated here — operators should assume the services that render ads see connection-refused or reset during the recreate, and should check the frontend path specifically. flagd sees ad's flag-evaluation traffic resume, which it logged no errors handling [tr_f75ff8f53156]. product-catalog, checkout, recommendation and frontend-proxy are untouched by this action; if their alerts clear, that is evidence of a causal link that has not otherwise been established.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Two independent services alerted simultaneously, which is more than a single quiet latency warning and not dismissible. flagd appears as a shared candidate cause for ad, making a flag change a reasonable cheap prior.
